seed: Shannon Byrne Susko, CULTURAL: Team Core Values Discovery, and Discovering or Confirming your Team Core Values with your Whole Leadership Team (adapted from Jim Collins’ Mission to Mars), Metronomics. Byron Darlison, Values: How Not To Chase Your Tail (darlison.com).

slides.title: Who would you send to Mars?
slides.headline: Who would you send to Mars?
slides.support: The Martians want to meet the people who best show what is right, best and noble about your company.
body: They learn your values only by watching those people live them.
notes: This is the Mission to Mars exercise. It discovers the values the company already lives.
The team does it together, in the room, today.
Allow about 60 minutes for the whole exercise.

artwork.alt: Three neutral grey figures stand beside a small rocket. A fourth figure holds a clipboard and gestures toward them, choosing who boards. One of the three wears a green badge.

slides.title: Mission to Mars has five steps.
slides.headline: Mission to Mars has five steps.
notes: Walk the five steps once, so the team sees where the exercise ends.
The next slides take each step in turn.

artwork.alt: Five steps in a row. 1, pick three people: each leader picks three people not in the room and names the value each one lives. 2, share and cluster: say who and why, move similar values together, name each cluster. 3, vote: three votes each, on the clusters that best show your values. 4, test the top three: test each one and talk about anything left out. 5, agree the Core Values: name each value and write the behaviour it means.

slides.title: Pick three people.
slides.headline: Pick three people.
slides.support: Work on your own. Pick three people who are not in this room.
body: Beside it, write the value that person lives.
Add one example of them living it.
notes: Each leader works in private. Reveal when everyone is done.
The people must be outside the room, so nobody picks a colleague at the table.
Ask for behaviour the leader has seen, not a quality they admire in general.

slides.title: Share who you picked, and why.
slides.headline: Share who you picked, and why.
slides.support: Each leader says who they picked and why.
body: Name each cluster with a word or a phrase.
notes: The coach groups the notes as each leader presents.
A few words that describe the behaviour are enough for now. The names come at the end.

slides.title: Vote for the values that best show your company.
slides.headline: Vote for the values that best show your company.
body: Put your votes on the clusters that best show your company’s values.
Stack them on one cluster, or spread them.
notes: Tally the votes for each cluster. The three with the most votes go forward.

slides.title: A value is a name and the behaviour it means.
slides.headline: A value is a name and the behaviour it means.

panels.heading: Own the outcome
panels.support: We take full responsibility for results, not effort or intent.

notes: These are the example company’s Core Values. Use them to show the form: a short name, then the behaviour.
Do not recommend adopting them. The team’s values come from the people it just named.
Watch for a value with no clear behaviour behind it.

slides.title: Agree your Core Values.
slides.headline: Agree your Core Values.
slides.support: Name each value. Write the behaviour it means.
body: Not aspirational. How your best people already act.
notes: The wording does not have to be perfect today. Agree the name and the behaviour, then refine the words as homework.
Homework: share the Core Values with the whole team.

slides.title: Go deeper on Core Values before the next session.
slides.headline: Go deeper on Core Values before the next session.
notes: Scan to open each page on darlison.com.
The first article shows how to describe each value at three levels of behaviour. It also shows how to hire on the values.
The second article and the prompt pressure-test each value against real stories.
